title: Australia is a regional maritime power. It should act like it | The Strategist
paragraphs: As Australia seeks to rebuild much of its aged naval fleet, it should also look to rebuild how it perceives itself in the Indo-Pacific. Australia is and has always been a regional maritime power, even if its capability has at times not kept pace with that statement. Australian leaders should not refer to Australia as having a small navy or seek to downplay our regional influence. Quite the contrary, they should lean into Australia having confidence as a regional maritime power.

It’s easy to predict the sniggering responses to the above statement. As a nation, Australians have rarely been comfortable with confidence. Many will point to Australia’s historically small surface combatant fleet or its ageing submarines. Both are valid critiques. But maritime power is not measured by ships alone. It is also measured by influence. And influence in the maritime domain goes beyond capability: it’s built on relationships.

Australia is a regional maritime power, and our regional partners have expectations of Australia to fulfil that role. The capability will come; it’s the influence Australia should focus on harnessing now.
